info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package allowance is how much a plan lets you do without paying, and how much of it you have left in the window that holds you.

get.summary: Answers what the CALLER has left of their plan's free-call allowance in the window that holds them, and the instant that window reopens.
get.description:
Answers what the CALLER has left of their plan's free-call allowance in the window
that holds them, and the instant that window reopens.

This is the number a product shows beside the composer — "2 of 3 left" —
and the moment to offer a plan is when it reaches zero. It READS: asking does not
spend, so a page that polls it costs the caller nothing. A Free person's window is
a session that opens at their first call after the last one ended and runs five
hours; while none runs, resets is 0 and the next call opens one.

A bounded caller is POOLED: the Free plan is limited usage from one pool every
free user shares — the platform's vendor accounts for free models — so the answer
says so (pooled) and carries that pool's standing: available, busy or exhausted,
and when it refills. The pool is read from the process that spends it and is
absent when that process does not answer, never guessed. A paid plan is not
pooled and carries no pool: its usage is metered in money.

The subject is the caller's own, resolved from the verified credential, and can
never be named in the request — so this is a mirror, not a lookup of someone else.
An unauthenticated caller is refused: there is no allowance without someone to
hold it.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

limit.description: calls the plan allows in Window; 0 = unbounded

plan.description: the tier the limit came from

pool.description:
Pool is that shared pool's standing, where it could be read. Absent when the
subject is not pooled, and when the process that holds it did not answer —
never a guess.

pooled.description:
Pooled says the calls counted here are served from the pool every free user
shares — the platform's vendor accounts for free models — rather than from
the subject's own plan. True exactly where a window bounds the subject.

resets.description:
Resets is the instant THAT window reopens, unix seconds: the next UTC hour or
midnight, or a session's start plus its length — exact, to the second, from
the call that opened it. 0 for a session that is not running: it opens at the
next call.

spent.description:
Spent says the ceiling refuses: on a take, that THIS call was refused and
nothing was counted; on a read, that the next call would be.

start.description:
Start is when the session this answer counts in opened, unix seconds: on a
take, the session the call was counted in, which a give names back
(AllowanceIn.Start); on a read, the session running. 0 where no session bounds
the subject or none runs.

used.description:
Used is how many free calls this subject has been admitted in the window
ending at Resets. A call counts when it is admitted, whatever its upstream then
does; a refused call counts nothing. It stops AT Limit rather than climbing
past it, so Limit-Used is what remains and never goes negative.

window.description:
Window is which ceiling these numbers describe — "hour", "session" or "day" —
because a caller can be held to more than one and only one of them is the
answer. A session is the Free plan's: it opens at the subject's first call
after the last one ended and runs five hours (ai_plan_session_hours). It is
the window that REFUSED where one did, and otherwise the one with least left,
so Limit-Used is always the number that will actually stop them next. Empty
where no window bounds the subject at all.

resets.description:
Resets is when the pool refills, unix seconds: set when it is exhausted,
and when it is busy for less than a minute. Absent otherwise.

state.description:
State is "available" (every account takes free requests), "busy" (some
account is at its vendor limit, or all are and one is back within a minute)
or "exhausted" (none is until Resets).

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
